page.layout: One page of text in a single column, with a marginal note at the upper right beside the Scripture quotation. Running head at top with page number at top right.

main_text.head: VERSVS XI.

p.i: Dixerunt ad eum: Quid faciemus ti-bi,ut fileat mare a nobis? Nam mare ibat & intumescebat.

main_text.p: 1. Sontes eò adducedi sunt, ut nulla se iniuria affici intelligant,cum poenas dare coguntur. Peccant itaq; magistratus,qui sic saeuiunt in reos,ut fatali casu se opprimi putent,non autem poenas scelerum se dare animaduertat,cum nemo sit qui de magnitudine peccatorum,& de ira Dei aduersus illa, de lege diuina,miseros erudiat.

2. Si adhibeatur grauis & tempestiua conscientiae appellatio,fructuilla non cerebit,siue eos qui resipiscunt, siue τὰς ἀμε- μετανοήτως spectes. Nam illi quidem,cum se peccauisse intelligat, iram Dei portabut, & Deo gloriam dabunt, spectatores autem & exemplo tristissimo & exhortatione a licentia peccandi dehortabuntur:hi uero,ut maxime se reos esse profiteri recusent,tamen in cordibus suis couincentur.
3. Conscientiae appellationem αὐτοψίαν, & sensus publice,ob unius noxa,grassantium poenarum, efficacissimam reddit.

page.notes: Right margin note "Lectio 19. 19. Decembr. 1580." is partly doubtful: the first number is read as 19 [?]. Greek in paragraph 2 ("τὰς ἀμε- μετανοήτως") and the Greek word in paragraph 3 ("αὐτοψίαν") are uncertain in their final letters; they are not confirmed. "Sontes eò", "tibi" and "efficacissimam" are as printed; the long s is written as plain s. Paragraph 2 "fructuilla" appears as printed and may be a misprint for "fructu illa". Mixed-type words in the middle of the page are read with some doubt.
